content: Inhibition of GSK3β by lithium ion significantly abolishes the onset of PTZ-induced seizure in Wwox-/- mice (report quoting its knowledge base; constitutive Wwox-null, provoked PTZ threshold)
anchor: L10, L18, L65, L113 (Summary; F001; F007; Evidence Base)
note: Called the single strongest and only firmly established benefit; framed as GSK-3β inhibition.

content: The lithium readout is a provoked threshold assay (PTZ challenge), not spontaneous recurrent seizures of the kind dominating the human disease.
note: Stated repeatedly as a qualification.

content: Lithium is pharmacologically non-selective: IMPase, IPPase and GSK-3β are all inhibited at therapeutic concentrations (quoted from a pharmacodynamics review), so inositol-depletion and GSK-3 theories both apply.
note: Quote: "all inhibited by lithium at therapeutic concentrations".

content: Lithium inhibits both GSK-3 isoforms at therapeutic concentrations (dual-isoform inhibition).
note: No separate citation given for the isoform statement.

content: Inositol-depletion and GSK-3 arms of lithium action are experimentally convergent because inhibiting inositol synthesis itself inactivates GSK-3; hence the GSK-3β-attributable fraction cannot be isolated with lithium.
note: Cited as support; sources not described beyond the one clause.

content: Lithium validates GSK-3β as a target but does not prove GSK-3β inhibition is the mechanism or sufficient; it validates the target, not the drug.
anchor: L10, L20, L103, L152 (Summary; F001; Model; Conclusion)
note: Internal tension with L152 sentence on attribution (see E63).

content: Lithium says nothing about spontaneous seizures, the clinically relevant drug-resistant WOREE phenotype; no published test of any GSK-3 intervention on spontaneous seizures; stated as the largest gap and the justification for the experiment.
note: Absence claim with no stated search perimeter.

content: The three feared adverse axes (Wnt/β-catenin dysregulation, impaired neuronal maturation, impaired myelination) are largely on-target consequences of GSK-3β inhibition, converging on the β-catenin branch, all developmental-window phenomena.
note: Described as the central and "somewhat uncomfortable" conclusion.

content: GSK-3β is the kinase of the β-catenin destruction complex; inhibiting it by any means stabilizes β-catenin and activates canonical Wnt signalling.
note: Presented as general background.

content: Report quotes "accumulation of β-catenin in the nucleus of GSK3-βi-treated" cells as showing that a substrate-competitive GSK-3β peptide inhibitor raises nuclear β-catenin.
note: Verifier (vf-09): the quoted words are a Methods description; the result is for one peptide (L803-mts), 100 uM, human dental pulp stem cells. Used by the report as proof that Wnt activation is intrinsic to the target.

content: Canonical Wnt/β-catenin is a negative regulator of oligodendrocyte maturation and remyelination and a gatekeeper of neural-progenitor fate.
note: General premise carried from non-WWOX literature.

content: Inhibiting Wnt/β-catenin "reversed the effects of CPZ on OPCs differentiation" and promoted remyelination.
note: Cuprizone demyelination setting (CPZ); species not stated in report.

content: Pharmacological modulation of Wnt/GSK-3β shapes oligodendrocyte differentiation through β-catenin-dependent transcription.
note: Direction of effect for GSK-3β inhibition not specified in the report.

content: WWOX-deficient models already display impaired oligodendrocyte maturation and hypomyelination.
note: WWOX datum, via knowledge base.

content: Driving β-catenin up via GSK-3β inhibition is predicted to worsen the myelination deficit of the disorder: an on-target liability, not an off-target accident.
note: Limitations section admits it is predicted not measured (E58).

content: Because the β-catenin branch lies downstream of GSK-3β kinase activity, the harms cannot be escaped by isoform selectivity alone, nor by "more selective kinase block".
anchor: L12, L27, L40, L152 (Summary; F003 title; F005; Conclusion)
note: Tension with F004 isoform-specific synaptic functions (E26).

content: Strategy 1: act upstream of the branch point by restoring WWOX itself (neuronal AAV9-WWOX) so seizures and myelination are corrected together without over-driving Wnt.
anchor: L14, L71, L74, L109 (Summary; F008; table)
note: Ranked first; "None (restorative)" for β-catenin liability.

content: Strategy 2: target β-catenin-independent excitability substrates of GSK-3β (PI4KIIα→NMDA/AMPA-receptor; PSD-95/KLC-2) controlling excitatory synaptic drive; liability "avoided by design".
anchor: L14, L75, L109 (Summary; F008 table; Model)
note: Ranked second.

content: Strategy 3: partial or substrate-competitive and/or time-gated GSK-3β inhibition, treating the chronic seizure phenotype after perinatal myelination and migration windows close; liability "mitigated, not eliminated".
note: Ranked third.

content: Because β-catenin destruction has a threshold character, partial inhibition can plausibly raise seizure threshold while leaving enough GSK-3β activity to keep β-catenin phosphorylated and degraded; full ATP-competitive blockade would close this window.
note: Hedged with "plausibly"; relies on E56 assumption.

content: Substrate-competitive GSK-3 inhibitors "can fulfill the requirement for selectivity and allow fine tuning of the degree of inhibition"; "moderate inhibition... provides more favorable outcome than complete inhibition".
note: Context of the source (disease/system) not given.

content: Temporal dissociation: dosing after the perinatal myelination and migration windows should preserve the anti-seizure effect while sparing developmental β-catenin-branch harms.
note: Presupposes seizures persist and respond after the windows; not tested.

content: The adverse arms (oligodendrocyte maturation, neuronal migration, progenitor differentiation) occur in defined perinatal windows, whereas seizures are chronic.
anchor: L12, L30, L40, L108 (Summary; F003; F005; Model)
note: Window timing asserted from KB; no timing source quoted.

content: GSK-3β stabilizes synaptic NMDA receptors and regulates AMPA-receptor surface expression via PI4KIIα phosphorylation; substrates KLC-2, PSD-95 and tau act in long-term depression; CT99021 reduces NMDAR-mediated currents.
note: Non-WWOX synaptic physiology; species/preparation not stated.

content: The PI4KIIα/NMDAR/AMPAR and PSD-95/KLC-2/tau branches are molecularly separable from the Wnt/β-catenin output; the plausible location of a "useful" target engageable without touching β-catenin.
note: Called "the most mechanistically encouraging finding".

content: GSK3α, but not GSK3β, is required for [NMDAR-dependent] LTD via tau-mediated spine anchoring, dissected with "novel isoform-selective drugs": isoform specificity at the synapse.
anchor: L35, L109, L121 (F004; Model; Evidence Base)
note: Bracketed insertion by the report. Shows GSK3α, not β, in LTD, which complicates use as a β-branch argument.

content: In WWOX models the excitability defect is measured: elevated EPSC amplitude in layer II/III pyramidal neurons, reduced inhibition, intrinsic hyperexcitability converging on neocortical bursting.
note: WWOX datum via KB; no PMID given.

content: The KB flags the GSK-3β to neocortical-hypersynchrony link as having unmapped intermediates; whether the benefit runs via PI4KIIα/NMDAR, β-catenin or another substrate in WWOX cortex is unestablished and inferred from non-WWOX synaptic physiology.

GSK-3β/β-catenin gates neural-progenitor fate: reduced GSK-3β activity stabilizes β-catenin and sustains proliferation at the expense of differentiation; GSK-3β activity promotes cell-cycle exit and differentiation.
note: Demonstrated in the DISC1 system.

content: DISC1 knockdown reduces progenitor proliferation, causing premature cell-cycle exit and differentiation; DISC1 inhibits GSK3β; "GSK3 inhibitors normalize progenitor proliferation" (quoted with ellipses).
note: Quoted passage is long and elided; non-WWOX system.

content: Neuronal maturation disturbance is a third on-target liability of GSK-3β inhibition acting through the β-catenin branch (progenitor proliferation/differentiation balance).
note: Predicted not measured in WWOX models (E58).

content: Model for the discriminating experiment: neuronal (Nex/Nestin-Cre) Wwox-deletion mice with spontaneous seizures and myelin defects, complemented by constitutive Wwox-null PTZ paradigm for provoked threshold.
note: Genotype and Cre-driver specifics attributed to KB.

content: Arm 1: lithium as the non-selective reference.
Arm 2: selective ATP-competitive GSK-3β inhibitor at full target engagement (e.g. CT99021/CHIR-class).
note: CT99021 is called selective GSK-3β inhibitor; elsewhere "selective GSK-3 inhibitor".

content: Arm 3: substrate-competitive GSK-3 peptide (L803-mts) enabling tunable partial inhibition.
note: L141 does name the arm ("substrate-competitive partial") in the six-arm list; the earlier note was wrong. Tension: L803-mts raised nuclear beta-catenin in the cited peptide paper (E10) while the report uses it as its tunable partial-inhibition arm.

content: Arm 4: low-dose/partial selective GSK-3β.
note: Predicted to dissociate benefit from harm.

content: Arm 5: selective GSK-3β dosed only after the perinatal myelination/migration window.
note: Predicted to dissociate benefit from harm.

content: Arm 6: an inositol-depletion mimic with no GSK-3 action, to isolate lithium's off-target arm (off-target subtraction).
note: No compound named. Tension with E05 (inositol inhibition itself inactivates GSK-3), so "no GSK-3 action" may be unattainable.

content: Genetic specificity control: cross inhibition-resistant constitutively active GSK-3β-S9A knock-in onto Wwox-null background; "expression of constitutively active GSK3β, but not GSK3α"; abolished rescue would prove on-target GSK-3β.
anchor: L55, L123, L144 (F006; Evidence Base; Follow-up)
note: Cited quote is a partial phrase. Logic of a constitutively active allele abolishing rescue is asserted, not argued. The Follow-up (L141) says the S9A cross is applied "where relevant" (see E85).

content: USEFUL readouts in every arm: spontaneous seizure frequency/duration on continuous video-EEG; neocortical slice bursting and EPSC amplitude; PTZ threshold.
COMPETING readouts in every arm: cortical β-catenin/Axin2; oligodendrocyte maturation (CC1+, MBP) and myelinated-axon counts; neural-progenitor/neuronal-maturation markers.
Separation criterion: an arm normalizing seizures/bursting while β-catenin/Axin2, myelin and maturation stay at Wwox-null baseline demonstrates dissociability; predicted for arms 4 and 5.
note: Report says "proven" in Follow-up (L143) versus "demonstrates" in F006.

content: Attribution logic: S9A knock-in abolishing the anti-seizure rescue proves on-target attribution; the inositol-mimic arm provides off-target subtraction.
Evidence table: induced (provoked) seizures have the strongest evidence (lithium abolishes PTZ seizures in Wwox-null mice).
Evidence table: spontaneous activity weakest/untested; measured phenotype is neocortical bursting, elevated EPSC amplitude, intrinsic hyperexcitability.
Evidence table: developmental outcomes are predicted double-edged; β-catenin accumulation can impair oligodendrocyte maturation and skew progenitor fate, both already deficient in WWOX.
note: Claim that progenitor/neuronal maturation is already deficient in WWOX has no separate source.

content: In EAE, lithium pretreatment "markedly suppressed the clinical symptoms... and greatly reduced demyelination" (MOG35-55 mice); the report judges it immune-mediated and not transferable to WWOX cell-intrinsic developmental deficit; effects are model-specific.
anchor: L68, L124, L135 (F007; Evidence Base; Limitations)
note: Quote is longer than the shortened form here. The immune-mediated attribution is the report's inference.

content: Neonatal neuronal AAV9-WWOX "rescued brain hyperexcitability and seizures, hypoglycemia, myelination deficits, and the premature lethality and behavioral deficits of Wwox-null mice".
note: Verbatim phrase at L71 (quoted in part).

content: AAV9-WWOX corrects excitability and myelination simultaneously because it restores the scaffold rather than over-driving Wnt; the only intervention shown to fix both in the same animals.
note: Mechanism "restores the scaffold" is the report's reading.

content: Therapeutic hierarchy: 1 root-node WWOX restoration; 2 β-catenin-independent excitability targeting; 3 partial/substrate-competitive and/or time-gated selective GSK-3β; 4 lithium (non-selective, inositol depletion, systemic off-targets, on-target liability).
note: Ranking is the report's own.

content: Conventional anti-seizure medicines fail about 95% of WOREE patients, which keeps a mechanism-matched node attractive.

Model: GSK-3β as a branch point with a useful output (β-catenin-independent; PI4KIIα to NMDAR/AMPAR, PSD-95, KLC-2, tau; lowers drive, raises seizure threshold) and a harmful output (β-catenin stabilization; blocks oligodendrocyte maturation, skews progenitor fate, Wnt transcription dysregulation).
note: Schematic also places WWOX loss upstream of GSK-3β producing hyperexcitability, hypomyelination, maturation defects, seizures; WWOX-to-GSK-3β step not sourced.

content: Lithium pulls both levers at once and also depletes inositol, a third convergent mechanism; proof-of-target but unacceptable as mechanism-pure or chronically safe therapeutic.
note: Chronically safe judgement without a cited safety source.

content: The useful (excitability) branch is likely more sensitive to GSK-3β inhibition than the harmful (β-catenin) branch, so partial inhibition raises seizure threshold with β-catenin degradation intact.
note: Admitted unmeasured in the Limitations.

content: In principle a druggable node exists that touches excitability without touching β-catenin (partly GSK3α vs GSK3β separable at the synapse).
Differential sensitivity of useful versus harmful branch has not been measured and could be false, in which case no partial-inhibition window exists.
Isoform-selective GSK-3 pharmacology is maturing; genuinely GSK-3β-selective, CNS-penetrant "partial agonists" suitable for chronic pediatric dosing are not clinically available.
note: Wording "partial agonists" for an inhibitor class is odd. Clinical-availability claim has no search perimeter.

content: Myelination and maturation liabilities are predictions from Wnt/oligodendrocyte and Wnt/progenitor biology, not observations of GSK-3β inhibitors worsening myelin in WWOX models; direction well supported, magnitude unknown.

Secondary: test whether CT99021 lowers EPSC amplitude/NMDAR currents in Wwox-null layer II/III pyramidal neurons and whether PI4KIIα knockdown occludes the effect, to confirm the β-catenin-independent branch carries the benefit.
Secondary: dose-response the separation, quantifying GSK-3β occupancy versus seizure-threshold shift versus cortical β-catenin/Axin2 to test whether a differential-sensitivity window exists.
Secondary: include a neonatal AAV9-WWOX arm as gold-standard comparator that corrects both branches, quantifying how much of the AAV9 benefit any GSK-3β strategy recovers.
Pursue medicinal-chemistry development of substrate-competitive/isoform-selective GSK-3β tools suitable for chronic post-developmental-window dosing (β-catenin-sparing chemistry).
Conclusion: only lithium's provoked seizure-threshold rescue is firmly attributable to GSK-3β inhibition, though confounded by inositol depletion and dual-isoform inhibition.
note: Contradicts the F001 title "cannot be attributed to GSK-3β inhibition alone" in wording (see phase1_note).

content: GSK-3β (primary target of the investigation; kinase of the destruction complex).
GSK-3α isoform (synaptic LTD; inhibited by lithium; contrast with β).
Inositol monophosphatase (IMPase) and inositol polyphosphatase (IPPase), lithium's inositol-depletion targets.
PI4KIIα, PSD-95, KLC-2 and tau as GSK-3β substrates in excitatory synaptic drive/LTD.
β-catenin / Axin2 as the harm-branch node and the proposed competing readout.
Lithium (reference non-selective; abolishes PTZ seizures in Wwox-null mice; EAE protective in a different system).
CT99021 / CHIR-class selective GSK-3 inhibitor (ATP-competitive; reduces NMDAR currents).
L803-mts, substrate-competitive GSK-3 peptide inhibitor.
note: Report attributes the peptide to that PMID; peptide in item E10 is "GSK3-βi" (unnamed).

content: Unnamed substrate-competitive GSK-3β peptide inhibitor (GSK3-βi) raising nuclear β-catenin in treated cells.
Constitutively active GSK-3β-S9A knock-in (genetic tool, not a drug).
Unspecified inositol-depletion mimic without GSK-3 action.
AAV9-WWOX gene replacement (neonatal, neuronal).
WWOX loss to GSK-3β dysregulation as the cause of hyperexcitability and seizures (schematic arrow and "mechanism-matched node").
note: Based on lithium PTZ data only; upstream link unsourced here.

content: GSK-3β inhibition to β-catenin stabilization to impaired oligodendrocyte maturation (myelin) in WWOX-deficient cells.
GSK-3β to PI4KIIα to NMDAR/AMPAR to excitatory drive to seizure threshold in WWOX cortex.
GSK-3β inhibition to β-catenin stabilization to altered neural-progenitor fate (neuronal maturation).
Lithium's anti-seizure effect may arise from inositol depletion or other substrates rather than GSK-3β inhibition; intermediate could be PI4KIIα/NMDAR, β-catenin or another substrate.

Interface fragments at top: "View full report" and a toggle glyph; not content, not acted on.
note: Not addressed to an agent beyond a UI label.

content: Report restates the question: compare induced seizures, spontaneous activity and developmental outcomes, and propose a discriminating experiment (task framing).
The F002 heading hedges the harm: "partly intrinsic to GSK-3β inhibition", against the Summary's "largely on-target" and the body's "intrinsic property".
note: Gradient of wording (partly / largely / intrinsic) recorded as one row; added after the blind audit.
